Subject: Randolph Urban Renewal Project
Richmond, Virginia Project Number Va. R-58
1. Name of Action: (Check One) (X) Administrative ( ) Legislative
2. Location of the Project
The Randolph area encompasses 380 acres of land in a highly urbanized area of Richmond, Virginia. The urban renewal area generally follows the boundaries given below:
To the north, the lots fronting on Parkwood Avenue
To the east, Linden Street and Hollywood Cemetery
To the south, Colorado Avenue
To the west, Byrd Park and, north of the Downtown Expressway,
Stafford avenue.
3. Brief Description of Action
The subject project area is predominantly residential in character (61.9% of the total area), and existing development occupies 79.4 percent of the entire area. Randolph contains 2,290 principal structures, of which a total of 669 buildings (29.2%) have been found to be substandard to an extent warranting clearance and 64 buildings (2.8%) exert blighting influences on the area. In all 1,833 structures or 80.0 percent have been classified as substandard with major, intermediate or minor deficiencies.
The Randolph Plan is proposed to be a redevelopment and conservation area. Of the 2,173 residential buildings in the area, containing a total of 3,287 dwelling units, 1,117 structures, or 1,613 dwelling units, will be cleared as a result of project action. Fifty-eight out of the 117 non-residential buildings will also be cleared. In the designated rehabilitation areas, 1,053 residential buildings (i.e. 1,674 dwelling units) and 52 non-residential buildings will be rehabilitated. It is the intent of the project to maintain the same approximate residential density that now exists in Randolph but to substantially upgrade the quality of housing and eliminate blight from the area.
